title: How much better is Claude than Gemini?
author: Least_Tumbleweed_599
selftext: Hello, I'm a hobbyist learning to make a game for fun. I wanted to use AI to assist me with it. I've done some research and it seems Claude is the best AI for coding. I already have a subscription to Gemini though and don't plan to replace it. I'm trying to figure out if Claude is so much better at coding than Gemini it's worth getting a subscription to that also. Thank you.

comments.author: BSwayzeYo
comments.body:
I started with Gemini. And then eventually realized that Gemini is excitable and REALLY likes to offer “new” or “extra” directions when working your code.
This was great at the beginning, but eventually I moved to Claude because Claude’s default is to just DO the thing. Claude almost never offers unsolicited directional advice or suggestions.

When I want to bounce ideas… I talk with Gemini.

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: Haven't tried Cloude yet but I agree, Gemini always tries to be ahead of you, sometimes it almost feels as I'm talking to a hyperactive person who just does whatever it wants to

comments.author: orange_wires
comments.body: If you get the Claude Pro subscription for $20/mo you can use Claude Code at the command line - a game changer! Previously I was cutting and pasting code into the LLM and even with help it took a few hours to get anything done, especially if the AI was being vague. But yeah Claude Code reads your entire codebase and just builds from a prompt, you can get up and walk the dog or whatever. That said, there's a proliferation of AI apps out there, I was just noting that I've seen like half a dozen people post today to look at their app. Getting any sort of traction is difficult in this environment, much harder than building these days. I won't link mine but if you look back through my comments you can find it... good luck!

replies.author: Least_Tumbleweed_599
replies.body: Oh, I'm not planning on selling it or anything. I'm really just doing it for fun. I mean, I might make it available for sale if it turns out good enough for me, but I'm mostly just doing this for fun. If it never makes a single dollar, I'll still have had fun.

replies.author: orange_wires
replies.body: Oh yeah, I mean, my little game is free and all that. It was mainly an experiment, and I'm learning a lot, not making any money. But just FYI you'll cut your development time 10-100x by using those AI coding apps.

replies.author: Least_Tumbleweed_599
replies.body: Just to clarify and make sure I'm understanding correctly. By AI coding apps, you're talking about something like Claude right? Or is there other, better software to use to build my game?

replies.author: orange_wires
replies.body: Yeah, that's what I mean. Another commenter has mentioned Gemini CLI (?), and I've also heard about OpenClaw but don't know anything about it.

replies.author: AcceptableArm8841
replies.body: Gemini cli can do the same thing and it's currently free. I use it when I run out of claude tokens lol

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
I personally dont notice much difference for building but Claude has an edge over Gemini when it comes to debugging and troubleshooting. I go to Claude when Gemini gets stuck

I suppose I can just use Claude 24/7 but I like my current combo

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body:
I've messed with most frontier models.

Iuno if im unlucky or skill issue but Gemini has broke my shit without fail in pretty major ways every time I throw it a bone. last time I gave it a writing task and it truncated a 5100 line file to 1300. before that, it was tasked to make a stat page UI. it somehow made the page run hot even when not in the menu, so combat runtime spiked frames because the closed stat page was trying to keep up with all the combat stat changes. it scares the hell out of me. currently I have it write narrative to a [draft.md](http://draft.md) and then I'll safely integrate it to the actual codebase after

comments.author: gomo666
comments.body: depend on what you need.... i guess

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: In my experience Gemini > Claude just takes a bit more prompt engineer to get consistent results with Gemini, Claude basically just has that built in but will still end up giving you generic outputs due to more and more people using it the only thing that sets any if the AI's apart are how they auto complete your missing context and the tools available to the agents but again imo if you aren't putting in extra engineering efforts when using AI then just use whatever feels the best to you if you are getting good results with gemini stick with it and learn more about it rather then jumping form AI to AI Ive tried Claude once with a standard test I do to new models for a personal use case and was not impressed by it what so ever

comments.author: Fic_Machine
comments.body:
Gemini is good on the chatbox. The Gemini extension in visual studio is horrible, or at least it was a month ago when I tried.

Claude is great, but you hit the limit very fast on a large codebase. It has also been dumbed down over the last few days due to Anthropic not having enough compute. 

I also like Cursor a lot. Their proprietary model is on par with Sonnet and has much more generous limits.

replies.author: SaltResident9310
replies.body: I'm kinda disillusioned with Claude because of the very restrictive limits. Is Cursor a better value for the money?

comments.author: Pretend_Prior_8423
comments.body:
I only found Gemini good for art. But they've recently drastically reduced the daily limit. 
Claude is a great coder. I asked it to do something, it did it, and said hey, here's some extra lovely stuff you might want too.
Deepseek is pretty good too.

comments.author: meischix
comments.body: They have different purposes for me. I like Gemini better for brainstorming, research, and trend reports. I use Claude for building and documentation.

comments.author: Mustafag91
comments.body:
Try out Bezi AI... it's an agentic AI able to work within Unity Editor with Claude under the hood. 
Pretty nice thing, didn't see anything else like this on the market.

replies.author: Least_Tumbleweed_599
replies.body: I hadn't considered agentic AI yet, honestly I don't fully understand it, lol.

replies.author: Mustafag91
replies.body:
It's way easier to use than other options, you just installthe app and the plugin, connect it to your Unity project. 
Then you can write GDD in it, write Plans, for example for features, it can help you lay out the plan for yourself based on the GDD.
You can set it rules and references, on how to approach coding, communication and what not to do.
You can then click "Build" on a Plan and it will start doing stuff in Editor.

However it will take some time for you to adjust your workflow as it depends how it consumes credits.
You can tell it to lay down a plan in small chunks and tell YOU how and what to do, instead of it doing it.

replies.author: Least_Tumbleweed_599
replies.body: I looked it up, I see the pro has 800 credits a month. How much does that work out to be? It would kind of suck if it ran out in a weekend.

replies.author: Mustafag91
replies.body:
Well several people in discord have different usage, someone uses 130 credits in a prompt, someone 5... that's why it depends on you playing around and finding the gold spot for ya, they have documentation and tips also, but still mostly depends on you.
As they have 3 models to choose (basic, core and frontier (which is claude opus) and it uses the most credits yet people say it's really good.
What I found best for me, is telling it to plan down features in smaller chunks, and ask it to tell me how to do it, or if I want to let it build, it will be smaller credit usage.

comments.author: kalvinbastello
comments.body: Really wish I knew what is better. Been using gpt 5.3 codex which seems the best one I've used so far. Haven't used Claude

comments.author: One-Flatworm-6838
comments.body: Is no one using codex anymore? been using gpt extended thinking for refining the implementation slices + long term planning + prompt generation. codex für implementing slices, extended thinking gain for debugging. any UI placement work i am doing myself by explosing all values to modify. been working really well for me so far
